header: L8 · The technical writer who maintains generated docs · sonnet
verdict: Mostly met: 25 of 29 non-parked round-8 findings read as resolved at 8ecfbb2. Largest gap: 04 4.1 claims that fix hints and --help examples are checked by the rule 13 matcher, but rule 13 matches README and guide commands against journey entries of commands.yaml, so no check owns the claim. No Blocking finding.

findings.defect: 04 4.1 says every command line in a fix hint and in a --help example is matched against the command definitions by the matcher of ADR 0001 rule 13, and the cluster resolution says ADR 0001 needs no change. Rule 13 covers README.md and docs/guide/ only, and compares each command with an entry of the page's journey in e2e/scenarios/commands.yaml, word by word; there is no journey for an error table row, and the target is not the command definitions.
findings.scenario: A PR renames romeu sync --overwrite-drift. T008 and T086 implement what 04 4.1 and the docs row of 10.2 say; the rule 13 matcher cannot take a hint (no journey, hints carry placeholders and flags that no commands.yaml entry lists), so the implementer either extends rule 13 on the decisions surface unasked or builds nothing. The stale hint ships and the operator at exit 4 runs a dead flag; 10 10.8 calls the hint 'reviewed', which is review only.
findings.change: Name the real mechanism in 04 4.1 and the docs row of 10.2: a test over the generated command definitions that parses each hint and --help example (command, subcommand, flags) and fails on an unknown one, as 12 12.3 already does for SKILL.md. Drop the pointer to rule 13, or amend rule 13 through a record. Carry it in T008.

findings.defect: The index row says tools/release writes the link to the docs at the release tag into the release notes, and the README install section links them. 12 12.6, the section that owns the notes, says nothing about that link, and plan T088 lists neither the link nor the Upgrading section of 12.6.
findings.scenario: T088 implements 12 12.6 and the Upgrading section; the docs link is absent from every implementing section, so v1.0.0 notes ship without it and a v1.1 reader follows the README into main's docs, the exact failure L8-3 raised.
findings.change: Add one sentence to 12.6 (notes open with a link to docs/ at the tag) and one acceptance line each in T088 for the link and the Upgrading section; keep the index row as the deferral of anything beyond the link.

findings.defect: Doctor checks and warnings are rows 'by slug and with no id'. Preflight step 5 makes the pre checks sbx-global-secret, sbx-broad-allow, home-symlink, auto-trust and vscode-trust fail a mutating command with exit 2, yet 4.1 says every error has an RJ id and the output form is 'error RJ-<nnn> <slug>'. Only signing-socket has an id (RJ-204). The 'recovered in' column of 12.3 is defined 'for each id', so these slugs have no guide anchor either.
findings.scenario: A new operator runs romeu sync at J1 and meets vscode-trust. The text form needs an id that the table cannot give, so T008 invents one or prints none; the page the operator is sent to has no recovery section and no check sees the gap.
findings.change: Give the five pre checks (and any other doctor check that stops a command) ids in 4.4 with their exit code, or state the output form for an id-less row, and extend the 'recovered in' rule to every failing row. Warnings may stay id-less.

findings.defect: The 'recovered in' column of the error table (a docs/guide anchor or 'none: <reason>') is defined only in 12.3, 12.8 and the docs row of 10.2. The pages that specify the table, 04 4.1 (fields, --json form) and 04 4.4 (the rows until T008), do not list it, and T008, which implements 04 4.1 and 12.3, does not require it. T094 still says 'no check reads which error ids a page names'.
findings.scenario: T008 builds the table from 04 4.1 and the 4.4 rows with no recovered-in field; the docs check of T086 then fails every id for an empty cell, or the field is added in the wrong place.
findings.change: Add the field to the Error ids row of 04 4.1 (and say whether --json carries it), a column or a rule for the rows of 4.4, an acceptance line in T008, and correct T094's review-only line to the anchor check.

findings.defect: T006 lands the rule 9 matcher over the spec and says the spec passes it. After the write pass the first mention of a record is not in the rule 9 link form in spec.md (ADR 0004 and ADR 0006 as links with no title, ADR 0008 bare in a deferred row), 01 1.7 ([ADR 0008] with no title), 04 4.1 (bare ADR 0001), 07 (bare ADR 0008), 10 (link text 'ADR 0007, Threat model' instead of the title) and 11 (bare ADR 0008). Only the 05 5.4 instance of L8-13 was fixed. I checked this by a script over code-span-stripped text, not by the real matcher.
findings.scenario: T006 merges the matcher; the first run on main fails on seven files the task did not touch, and the spec carries a red docs step into the next task.
findings.change: Sweep the spec pages once for first mentions with the rule 9 form (a mechanical edit), and run the matcher from T006 as the proof.

findings.defect: The resolution says the tools/ci docs header-row check is dropped. The docs row of 10.2 now adds it ('a spec page holding a table whose header row equals a generated reference table's', citing 03's opening), and 03's opening describes no such check. The resolution also says the replacement of the 03 tables is recorded as T021 acceptance; T021 does not list it (it lists only the generated pages).
findings.scenario: T086 implements a check the approved resolution removed and the 03 text does not define; T021 merges with the hand tables still in 03, which then disagree with project.md on the next field change.
findings.change: Delete the clause from the docs row, or define the check in 03; add the table replacement to the acceptance of T021.

findings.defect: 12.5 says the spec names no plan task. 03's opening names T021 and 04 4.4 names T008.
findings.scenario: The plan renumbers a task (it was rewritten in this pass); the citations point at the wrong task and no check resolves them.
findings.change: Replace each with the module or the event ('when the error table lands', 'the pull request that lands the project generator').

findings.defect: The completeness checks now keep one guide per journey after v1.0.0, but S10 and 10 10.5 do not say that the expected output of a guide step is checked by nothing: rule 13 compares command words only, and the CI scenarios run J2, J3b, J6, J7, J10 and J11 only.
findings.scenario: v1.2 changes the output of romeu salvage; every gate passes and the J6 guide shows the old output.
findings.change: Say in S10 that expected output in guides is [review], and that each change of output updates its guide in the same PR (10 10.8 already says it for a changed journey).

confidence: medium-high: each finding cites text I read at 8ecfbb2; the rule 9 list comes from a script and should be confirmed by the T006 matcher.
